name: Non-small cell lung cancer
theme: the ticket rack · ten drivers, one panel

meta.title: Non-small cell lung cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Non-small cell lung cancer (adenocarcinoma and squamous), stages I-IV, adult
meta.population: Adults with NSCLC - the leading cause of cancer death (about one in five US cancer deaths) and the most biomarker-fragmented solid tumor in this registry: ten driver tickets on one panel, three curative-intent eras colliding in stages I-III, and a metastatic menu where the single most consequential act is WAITING for the panel before starting immunotherapy. Adenocarcinoma and squamous histology are inputs, not separate specs; Pancoast tumors and LCNEC stay inside (notes); small-cell histology hard-routes to its own row, and bronchopulmonary carcinoid routes to the neuroendocrine family. Staged by TNM-9 (effective 2025 - N2a/N2b, M1c1/M1c2), which the NCI PDQ itself has not caught up to.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease with oncology's densest ticket rack. The metastatic readiness gate encodes the field's cardinal discipline: no ranking - and in the clinic, no pembrolizumab - until the molecular panel returns, because starting immunotherapy before finding an EGFR or ALK ticket costs real survival and real toxicity. Signature content: the driver-exclusive menus (each ticket opens exactly one branch); the EGFR first-line intensification ledger (osimertinib alone, with chemo - OS 47.5 vs 37.6 - or with amivantamab-lazertinib - OS significant over osimertinib…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: IASLC/AJCC TNM 9th edition (effective 2025-01-01 for lung: N2 subdivided N2a/N2b; M1c split M1c1/M1c2; T unchanged) - note: NCI PDQ still prints 8th-edition tables
meta.response: RECIST 1.1; pathologic response (pCR/MPR) after neoadjuvant therapy is the curative pathway's readout (CheckMate 816: 5-yr OS 95.3% in pCR patients)

Newly diagnosed.name: Surgery + perioperative immunochemotherapy (the CheckMate 816 / KEYNOTE-671 era)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 - EFS and OS met (CheckMate 816 final OS fresh, 2025)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: immunochemotherapy's ledger plus thoracic surgery; the pneumonitis rule applies on both sides of the operation
Newly diagnosed.patient: Immunotherapy woven around the operation - the approach that just posted its five-year proof: two-thirds alive at five years, and dramatically better when the pathology report comes back clean.
drugs: Nivolumab- or pembrolizumab-based perioperative immunochemotherapy + anatomic resection

Newly diagnosed.name: Surgery alone - with proven minimalism for the smallest tumors (CALGB 140503 / JCOG0802)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the operation and its recovery; sublobar spares lung function - the JCOG local-relapse arithmetic rides on the card
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the smallest tumors: surgery alone still cures most people - and two landmark trials proved that removing less lung works as well as removing a whole lobe.
drugs: Lobectomy or sublobar resection + nodal sampling

Newly diagnosed.name: Surgery + adjuvant osimertinib (ADAURA - the targeted-adjuvant era)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - DFS and OS met (OS HR 0.49)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: three years of a well-tolerated tablet (rash, diarrhea, rare pneumonitis and QT vigilance) appended to the surgical road
Newly diagnosed.patient: For resected EGFR-mutant cancer: three years of a daily tablet after surgery cut the risk of death in half - the clearest targeted-adjuvant win in any solid tumor.

Newly diagnosed.name: SBRT (medically inoperable stage I)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: prospective phase 2 (RTOG 0236); randomized surgery-comparison honestly absent
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a week of outpatient precision radiation; chest-wall and fatigue effects modest - the gentlest curative-intent card in the spec
Newly diagnosed.patient: For small tumors when surgery is not safe: a few days of pinpoint radiation controls the tumor itself about 98% of the time.

Newly diagnosed.name: Chemoradiation + durvalumab (PACIFIC - unresectable stage III's backbone)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS and OS met, 5-yr mature
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the chemoradiation season (esophagitis, fatigue) then a year of infusions; pneumonitis vigilance is the through-line
Newly diagnosed.patient: For stage III disease that cannot be operated on: chemotherapy with radiation, then a year of immunotherapy - the combination that lifted five-year survival past forty percent.
drugs: Platinum doublet + thoracic RT -> durvalumab consolidation

Newly diagnosed.name: Chemoradiation + osimertinib (LAURA - the EGFR stage III re-route, OS young)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS met (HR 0.16); OS immature (interim HR 0.81, flagged)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: chemoradiation then an open-ended tablet; pneumonitis vigilance doubled (radiation + TKI both carry it)
Newly diagnosed.patient: For EGFR-mutant stage III that cannot be operated on: the targeted tablet after chemoradiation held the cancer back seven times longer - with the honest note that its survival ledger is still filling in.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.evidence: teaching estimate (flagged); early-palliative-integration randomized in this very disease
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from antitumor therapy; breathlessness care is the central craft
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice with real numbers - and comfort care itself is proven therapy in lung cancer, woven into every option on this page.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: EGFR first line: the intensification menu (three approved roads, told straight)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: three FDA-approved 1L options (dates secondhand); preference wording not verified live
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized x3 - two with OS wins over the former standard
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: road-dependent: tablet-only gentleness (osi), chemo's season (FLAURA2), or the amivantamab ledger (infusion reactions, rash, VTE) - the choice IS the toxicity…
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For the most common lung cancer ticket: three proven first choices - the gentle tablet, the tablet plus chemotherapy (longer life, harder months), or the two-drug combination that beat the tablet itself (longer life, more side effects). The honest choice is about what you are willing to carry.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: EGFR exon 20: amivantamab + chemotherapy (PAPILLON)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS met; OS immature
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: infusion reactions (front-loaded), rash, VTE vigilance, plus the chemo backbone
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For the exon-20 variant that ordinary EGFR tablets miss: an antibody plus chemotherapy nearly doubled the time in control.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: ALK first line: the split crown (alectinib's OS receipt, lorlatinib's control)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: both FDA-approved 1L; preference wording not verified live (flagged)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (ALEX mature OS; CROWN unprecedented PFS, OS young)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: alectinib: myalgias, photosensitivity - famously livable; lorlatinib: lipids, weight, neurocognitive effects - the price of the deepest CNS control
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For ALK-positive cancer: tablets measured in years - one with the proven survival record, one holding the longest disease control ever measured in this disease (with its own side-effect personality).

Relapsed / recurrent.name: ROS1: repotrectinib (TRIDENT-1)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 1/2 single-arm (deep and durable; not randomized)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: dizziness (the class signature - dose-titrated), weight gain, neuropathy vigilance
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For the ROS1 ticket: a tablet with responses in four of five people and control measured in years.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: KRAS G12C, second line: the still-provisional ticket (the saga rides along)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: accelerated approvals (2021/2022); conversions unresolved - the ledger's lung chapter
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: randomized vs docetaxel (PFS only, modest); accelerated approvals with disputed confirmatories
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: diarrhea and hepatotoxicity (monitored); gentler than docetaxel, which is the honest bar it beat on PFS alone
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The most common driver finally has tablets - honest label: they work after chemotherapy-immunotherapy (not instead of it yet), responses come in about a third, and their approvals are still formally provisional while the proving arguments continue.
drugs: Sotorasib or adagrasib (KRAS G12C inhibitors), post-chemo-IO

Relapsed / recurrent.name: MET exon 14: capmatinib / tepotinib (both fully approved)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: both FULLY approved (conversions completed - dates secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 2 single-arm x2, converted to full approvals
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: peripheral edema (the class signature), nausea, creatinine drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For the MET ticket, common in older patients: tablets with responses in two of three - and approvals that graduated to permanent on schedule.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: RET: selpercatinib (LIBRETTO-431 - the randomized 1L win)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: hypertension, transaminitis, QT monitoring - a monitored but livable tablet
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For the RET ticket: a tablet that beat chemotherapy-immunotherapy head-to-head, holding the cancer back more than twice as long.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: HER2-mutant: three approvals in eighteen months (zongertinib leads)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: three accelerated approvals 2022-2026 (dates secondhand); conversions pending across the board
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 1/2 cohorts (accelerated); the confirmatory chapter is unwritten
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: zongertinib: diarrhea/rash (oral); T-DXd: the ILD discipline travels from the breast trainers to here unchanged
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A ticket that went from one option to three in under two years - tablets now lead, with responses in three of four people, and every card honestly marked 'approval still provisional.'

Relapsed / recurrent.name: BRAF V600E / NTRK: the doublet and the tumor-agnostic pioneers
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: BRAF doublet: pyrexia, skin; TRK inhibitors: dizziness, weight - both livable tablet roads
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Two of the rarer tickets: tablet combinations with responses in about three of four people, durable for years in many.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Pembrolizumab alone (KEYNOTE-024 - the TPS>=50% receipt)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: immune-related events (thyroid, skin, colitis, pneumonitis) without chemotherapy's - the gentlest driver-negative road
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For high immune-marker disease without a driver ticket: immunotherapy alone - no chemotherapy - doubled five-year survival.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Chemo-immunotherapy (KEYNOTE-189/407 - the any-PD-L1 backbone)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 - OS met, 5-yr mature
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: chemotherapy's season plus the immune ledger; the 2L bar this menu's challengers must beat is docetaxel's ~11-12-month median (stated so the tornado has a floo…
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The workhorse for driver-negative disease at any immune-marker level: chemotherapy plus immunotherapy, with five-year survivors now counted in real numbers.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Dual immunotherapy (CheckMate 227/9LA - the PD-L1-negative long tail)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 - OS met, 5-yr mature, PD-L1-negative subgroups the teaching point
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the dual-checkpoint ledger: more colitis, endocrinopathy, hepatitis than single-agent roads - the long tail's tax
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For disease with no immune marker at all - the group immunotherapy was supposed to fail - the double-immunotherapy road nearly tripled five-year survival, and most long survivors are off treatment entirely.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: teaching estimate (flagged); early-integration randomized in this disease
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: none from therapy; breathlessness care is the craft
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Comfort-focused care is proven therapy in lung cancer - chosen alone it is a real road with real numbers, and chosen alongside treatment it makes the treatment better.

refs.label: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer - current version at least v5.2026 (2026-03-13, per the metastatic patient book's own citation; JNCCN printed v4.2026; nccn.org 403 - version SECONDHAND, confirm)
NCCN Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors (JNCCN Insights - explicitly covers bronchopulmonary/thymic NETs): the carcinoid gate's routing authority

NCI PDQ: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Treatment (HP, updated 2025-05-15, loaded live 2026-08) - NOTE: its staging tables still print AJCC 8th edition; do not source staging from it (the lag itself is taught)

IASLC TNM-9 N-descriptor proposal: N2 subdivided N2a (single-station) / N2b (multi-station) with robust prognostic separation - effective with TNM-9, 2025-01-01. J Thorac Oncol 2023 (PMID 37866624 anchors)
IASLC TNM-9 M-descriptor proposal: M1c split into M1c1 (single extrathoracic organ system) / M1c2 (multiple) - effective 2025. J Thorac Oncol 2024 (PMID 38320664)

Lindeman et al. CAP/IASLC/AMP updated molecular testing guideline for lung cancer TKI selection (triple-published). J Mol Diagn 2018 - the panel's founding document; the newer tickets (G12C, exon20 drugs) ride on NCCN
Kalemkerian et al. ASCO endorsement of the CAP/IASLC/AMP testing guideline (adds stand-alone ROS1/BRAF; RET/ERBB2/KRAS/MET in larger panels). JCO 2018;36:911-9
Altorki et al. CALGB 140503: sublobar resection noninferior to lobectomy for peripheral <=2 cm N0 - 5-yr OS 80.3% vs 78.9%. NEJM 2023;388:489-98

Saji et al. JCOG0802: segmentectomy vs lobectomy (<=2 cm, CTR>0.5) - 5-yr OS 94.3% vs 91.1% (superior) at the price of doubled local relapse (10.5% vs 5.4%). Registry UMIN000002317 (no NCT - Japanese registry). Lancet 2022;399:1607-17
Tsuboi et al. ADAURA overall survival: adjuvant osimertinib (resected EGFR-mutant IB-IIIA) - OS HR 0.49 in both populations; 5-yr OS 88% vs 78% (IB-IIIA). NEJM 2023;389:137-47
Forde et al. CheckMate 816 primary: neoadjuvant nivolumab-chemo - pCR 24.0% vs 2.2% (OR 13.94); EFS HR 0.63. NEJM 2022;386:1973-85
Forde et al. CheckMate 816 final overall survival (NEJM 2025): 5-yr OS 65.4% vs 55.0% (HR 0.72, p=0.048) - and 95.3% in the pCR stratum: the checkpoint's defining number. NEJM 2025;393
Spicer et al. KEYNOTE-671 overall survival: perioperative pembrolizumab - OS HR 0.72 (p=0.0052), 36-mo OS 71% vs 64%. Lancet 2024;404:1240-52

Timmerman et al. RTOG 0236: SBRT for medically inoperable stage I - 3-yr primary tumor control 97.6%, 3-yr OS 55.8%. JAMA 2010;303:1070-6 (operable-patient question honestly unanswered: STARS/ROSEL pooled n=58 only)
Spigel et al. PACIFIC 5-year: chemoradiation + durvalumab consolidation - 5-yr OS 42.9% (placebo ~33%, digit flagged pending re-confirmation); median OS 47.5 vs 29.1 mo (HR 0.72). JCO 2022;40:1301-11

Lu et al. LAURA: osimertinib after chemoradiation (EGFR-mutant unresectable stage III) - PFS 39.1 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.16; OS immature (interim HR 0.81, 20% maturity - the card's flag). FDA approval 2024-09 (secondhand). NEJM 2024;391:585-97
Ramalingam et al. FLAURA: 1L osimertinib - OS 38.6 vs 31.8 months (HR 0.80, p=0.046). NEJM 2020;382:41-50

Janne et al. FLAURA2 final OS (NEJM 2025): osimertinib + chemotherapy - OS 47.5 vs 37.6 months (HR 0.77, p=0.02); grade >=3 AEs 70% vs 34% - the intensification arithmetic on one line. NEJM 2025;394:27-38

Yang et al. MARIPOSA final OS (NEJM 2025): amivantamab + lazertinib vs osimertinib - OS HR 0.75 (p=0.005), median NR vs 36.7, 3-yr OS 60% vs 51%; grade >=3 80% vs 52%, 10% discontinuation - the first regimen to beat osimertinib on survival, price included. NEJM 2025;393:1681-93

Zhou et al. PAPILLON: amivantamab + chemo for EGFR exon 20 insertions (1L) - PFS 11.4 vs 6.7 (HR 0.40), ORR 73% vs 47%; mobocertinib's withdrawal (2023) is the pocket's ledger note. NEJM 2023;389:2039-51
Mok et al. ALEX mature analysis: alectinib 1L - PFS 34.8 vs 10.9 months; 5-yr OS 62.5% vs 45.5% - the ALK crown's survival half. Ann Oncol 2020;31:1056-64

Solomon et al. CROWN 5-year: lorlatinib 1L - median PFS not reached vs 9.1 months, HR 0.19; 5-yr PFS 60%; intracranial progression HR 0.06 - 'the longest PFS ever reported with any single-agent targeted therapy in advanced NSCLC'; OS immature. JCO 2024;42:3400-9
Drilon et al. TRIDENT-1: repotrectinib in ROS1+ NSCLC - TKI-naive ORR 79%, median PFS 35.7 months; G2032R activity. Approved 2023-11 (secondhand). NEJM 2024;390:118-31
Skoulidis et al. CodeBreaK 100: sotorasib (2L+) - ORR 37.1%, mDOR 11.1 months. NEJM 2021;384:2371-81

de Langen et al. CodeBreaK 200: sotorasib vs docetaxel - PFS 5.6 vs 4.5 (HR 0.66), no OS benefit. THE SAGA: ODAC 10-2 against the PFS's interpretability; CRL 2023-12; still accelerated with a 2028 confirmatory obligation; 960 mg validated (all regulatory items secondhand). Lancet 2023;401:733-46
KRYSTAL-12: adagrasib vs docetaxel - PFS 5.5 vs 3.8 (HR 0.58); full-approval conversion UNVERIFIED (treat as accelerated - flagged). Lancet 2025;406
Wolf et al. GEOMETRY mono-1: capmatinib for MET ex14 - ORR ~68% treatment-naive; converted to FULL approval 2022-08 (secondhand). NEJM 2020;383:944-57
Paik et al. VISION: tepotinib for MET ex14 - comparable activity; converted to FULL approval 2024-02 (secondhand). NEJM 2020;383:931-43

Zhou et al. LIBRETTO-431: 1L selpercatinib vs platinum-pemetrexed +/- pembro (RET fusion+) - PFS 24.8 vs 11.2 months (HR 0.46), ORR 84%; traditional approval 2022-09 (secondhand). NEJM 2023;389:1839-50

Zongertinib (Beamion LUNG-1): oral HER2 TKI - AA 2025-08; EXPANDED to 1L 2026-02, ORR 76% (11% CR); sevabertinib AA 2025-11 (ORR 71%) - three HER2-mutant approvals in 18 months, all provisional (all dates secondhand; sponsor/press-corroborated)
Goto et al. DESTINY-Lung02: T-DXd for HER2-mutant NSCLC - confirmed ORR 49% at 5.4 mg/kg; AA 2022-08, NO conversion found (flagged). The ILD discipline travels with the drug. JCO 2023;41:4852-63
Riely et al. PHAROS: encorafenib + binimetinib for BRAF V600E - ORR 75% treatment-naive; approved 2023-10 (secondhand). JCO 2023;41:3700-11
Drilon et al. Larotrectinib in TRK-fusion cancers - pooled ORR 75%; the first tumor-agnostic era's founding paper. NEJM 2018;378:731-9
Reck et al. KEYNOTE-024 5-year: pembrolizumab mono (TPS>=50%) - 5-yr OS 31.9% vs 16.3% (HR 0.62 despite 66% crossover). JCO 2021;39:2339-49
Garassino et al. KEYNOTE-189 5-year: pembro + pemetrexed-platinum (nonsquamous) - 5-yr OS 19.4% vs 11.3% (HR 0.60), benefit at every PD-L1 level. JCO 2023;41:1992-8
Novello et al. KEYNOTE-407 5-year: pembro + chemo (squamous) - 5-yr OS 18.4% vs 9.7% (HR 0.71). JCO 2023;41:1999-2006
Brahmer et al. CheckMate 227 5-year: nivolumab + ipilimumab - PD-L1-negative stratum 5-yr OS 19% vs 7%; two-thirds of 5-year survivors off all therapy. JCO 2023;41:1200-12
Reck et al. CheckMate 9LA 5-year: nivo+ipi + 2 chemo cycles - 5-yr OS 18% vs 11%; PD-L1-negative 22% vs 8%. Eur J Cancer 2024;211:114296

Xiong et al. HARMONi-2 (China): ivonescimab vs pembrolizumab (PD-L1+, 1L) - PFS 11.1 vs 5.8 months (HR 0.51); OS immature; China-only population - context for HARMONi-3, not US practice. Lancet 2025;405:839-49

Siegel et al. Cancer statistics 2026: lung cancer remains the leading US cancer killer (~124,990 deaths estimated; ~1 in 5 cancer deaths); overall 5-yr relative survival ~28% with by-stage figures pending SEER re-verification (fetch blocked). CA Cancer J Clin 2026

refs.label: El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

CISPLATIN-INELIGIBILITY CONSENSUS (the renal half): Galsky et al., 'A consensus definition of patients with metastatic urothelial carcinoma who are unfit for cisplatin-based chemotherapy' (Lancet Oncol 2011 - PMID 21376284, pubmed-eutils-verified 2026-08-27; also carried verbatim in the bladder trainer's galsky ref): any one of ECOG >=2, CrCl <60 mL/min, grade >=2 hearing loss, grade >=2 neuropathy, NYHA >=III defines cisplatin-unfit. The CrCl <60 criterion is the renal gate cisplatin-central regimens inherit.

honesty: Unverified statuses never carry the current date; every 'confirm' lives in the manifest staleness list.

The panel gate is the spec's soul: stage IV ranking is WITHHELD until the molecular panel returns, because the clinic's version of ranking early - starting immunotherapy before an EGFR/ALK result - is a real error with…
Ticket menus are exclusive and say so: a held driver closes every other targeted branch, and no targeted card claims superiority over cards it never shares a screen with.

The EGFR intensification menu is told as arithmetic, not advocacy: two roads beat the old standard on survival (FLAURA2 +9.9 months median; MARIPOSA HR 0.75 over osimertinib itself), both at real toxicity prices stated…

ALK's crown is split honestly: alectinib holds the verified 5-year OS (62.5%), lorlatinib the unprecedented control (5-yr PFS 60%, OS immature) - the ranked number is the receipt, the note is the frontier.

The regulatory ledger renders verbatim: sotorasib's saga (ODAC 10-2, CRL, still accelerated with a 2028 obligation), mobocertinib's withdrawal, HER2-mutant's three provisional approvals, MET's quiet double conversion -…

Evidence-maturity discipline throughout: five-year OS landmarks and mature medians rank; single-arm ORRs and young PFS wins (LAURA, PAPILLON, the ticket cohorts) display labeled; LAURA's flagged OS placeholder deliberat…
TNM-9 is the staging law here (N2a/N2b, M1c1/M1c2) - and the fact that NCI PDQ still prints the 8th edition is taught as a live lesson in guideline lag, not hidden.

The pneumonitis rule is universal: IO, radiation, TKI, and ADC cards all carry it, in the population with the least pulmonary reserve - new cough or breathlessness gets same-week attention on every single card.
Registry wins for status; the peer-reviewed paper wins for numbers; both are logged.
